subject: How to put fixed effects in lavaan SEM model?

messages.author: fad72ea718e74d71
messages.subject: How to put fixed effects in lavaan SEM model?
parts:
Here is the model I am trying to run in Stata:

gsem (m1<- x1 x2 x3 i.id i.time) ( m2<- x1 x2 x3 i.id i.time) (y<- m1 m2 x1 x2 x3 i.id i.time)

How can I estimates this model in lavaan? As u can see, the model includes firm fixed  effect and time fixed effect. Does anyone know how to add fixed effects terms in lavaan?

BTW, the dataset is evidently panel data. The first column is id, and the second column is time.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: How to put fixed effects in lavaan SEM model?
parts: How can I estimates this model in lavaan?
We aren't all Stata users, so you should provide enough detail (not just Stata syntax) to answer your question.
As u can see, the model includes firm fixed  effect and time fixed effect.
No, I can't see that.  There is an "i.time" variable, and there is an "i.id" variable, but no "firm" variable.
BTW, the dataset is evidently panel data. The first column is id, and the second column is time.

Evidently?  Are you saying these data are in long format?  SEM can handle panel data in wide format.  You can search for "autoregressive cross-lagged panel models", and add "lavaan syntax" too.  Here's one that came up in Google:  http://web.pdx.edu/~newsomj/semclass/ho_cross%20example%201.pdf
